races.title: State Senate, District 45
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mark Hollo
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 45 (Catawba and Caldwell counties) since January 2025. A physician assistant who worked at Family Care Center in Taylorsville and reached captain in the U.S. Air Force Reserve. Served in the NC House from 2005 to 2007 and from 2011 to 2015.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Mark Hollo was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no documented deeds or stated positions of his on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. The pages we had list his sponsored bills only as an empty table. We found no documented controversies, no endorsements, and no stated positions on data centers or development. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2024 or 2026.

qual.background: Served in the NC House (2005–07 and 2011–15, including vice chair of Appropriations in 2013–14) and has been in the NC Senate since 2025; career physician assistant and Air Force Reserve captain.
qual.why: He has roughly a decade of prior legislative service, including budget-writing work on Appropriations, and holds a state Senate seat now. His career work is in health care rather than law, policy or budget, so the score sits below the top of the range. The committee chair and vice-chair posts were not counted.

cands.name: Greg Cranford
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 45 in 2026. Graduated from UNC-Chapel Hill in 1981. Previously ran unsuccessfully for NC House District 89 in 2018, 2020 and 2024. No elected offices held.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter-guide recommendation from the 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' Sway voting group (Vote for Peace).
Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter-guide recommendation from the 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' Sway voting group (Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Greg Cranford was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or what he has done for work. We found no platform on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2020, 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. His only survey answers are from 2018, when he ran for a different office, and they cover health care, jobs and school testing. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no documented foreign ties.
